speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; to determine the cause, how many weeks old are you, and when did these symptoms first appear?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus. The presence of bilious vomiting in a newborn born only six hours ago is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise, and the family history of pyloric stenosis is a red herring for this specific acute presentation. Immediate surgical consultation is required.
